preamble: Affrication of the voiceless sibilant [s] to [ts] after a sonorant consonant (/n, l, r/), a fortition in which a brief stop closure develops at the transition from the sonorant. It is a regional feature of central and southern Italian (il sugo [ilˈtsuːɡo] in Ancona), and in many Basque dialects the fricative/affricate contrast is neutralized after nasals and liquids in favour of the affricate (Spanish verso > Goizueta Basque bèrtso 'poem').

examples.note: Post-sonorant /s/ affricates after /n, l, r/ both within words and across word boundaries; the affrication is not systematic in regional Italian and is more frequent in male speakers.
After a nasal or liquid the fricative/affricate contrast is neutralized in favour of the affricate.
Synchronic alternation: an auxiliary beginning with a fricative is affricated after /n/ and /l/.

sources: Tordini, O. (2020). Il consonantismo dell'italiano regionale di Ancona: prime indagini sperimentali. Quaderni di Linguistica e Studi Orientali 6: 257–277. https://oaj.fupress.net/index.php/bsfm-qulso/article/view/9702
Hualde, J. I., Lujanbio, O., & Zubiri, J. J. (2010). Goizueta Basque. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 40(1): 113–127. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100309990260
